messages:
maya (oncall): quick snapshot from my shift — saw a regen queue spike after the eu-west deploy around 19:12. 90th latency up ~120ms, small uptick in kvcache evictions. rolling mitigations applied and handing off.

oncall-bot: Incident detected: regen-queue-eu-west (ID: INC-2438). alerts: latency_p90 > 100ms, kvcache_eviction_rate doubled.

alex: thanks maya. did we push the autoscaler tweak in the deploy?

maya (oncall): yup—small autoscaler threshold change + prefetch enabled. i rolled back the autoscaler tweak at 19:18 which reduced new queue growth. prefetch still on, watching effect.

sam: put a temporary scale bump on dedicated-pool-eu by +2 nodes at 19:21 to buy time. metrics look like backlog draining now.

jordan: noted. i'll keep an eye on k/v miss rate and eviction churn; can revert prefetch if it keeps thrashing cache.

alex: can someone paste the quick command you used to roll back autoscaler? want it in the runbook.

maya (oncall): pasted below — one-liner we used in k8s control plane:
```bash
kubectl -n infra patch horizontalpodautoscaler autoscaler-regen -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":4,"maxReplicas":12}}'
```

sam: thanks. i've added a temporary alert suppression for noisy eviction alerts so we don't get paged repeatedly while backlog drains. will remove in 2h.

jordan: i'm going to run a small tracing diff to see whether specific model variants triggered the regen spike. will report if I find a hot path.

alex: heads-up — PR #432 (regen: revert autoscaler heuristic) ready for review, @jordan @sam. small tests added. if approved i'll merge and kick a controlled deploy in the morning.

maya (oncall): current blockers: none active — backlog is draining, p90 trending down. next steps:
- alex to get PR merged and schedule morning canary.
- jordan to follow up on tracing and confirm no variant-level regressions.
- sam to watch eviction churn and remove suppression once stable.

maya (oncall): handoff notes for next shift: check INC-2438 ticket for updates, link to dashboards: https://grafana.company.local/d/regen-eu, and replay logs under /ops/logs/regen/2026-03-17. if latency rises >100ms again, consider disabling prefetch or temporarily routing traffic to dedicated fallback pool.

alex: pinging @eng-runtime for review if anyone from that team is reading — PR small and time-sensitive. :pray:

sam: all good from my end — no further action unless churn restarts.

jordan: i'll post any tracing findings to this thread. good handoff, thanks maya. :thumbsup:

maya (oncall): thanks team — signing off. leaving the incident in monitored state, label set to "post-mitigations".
